I farm a small area, only 6.8 mu, and there are just two people in my household, so I will keep the plan simple and manageable. I already know this land and I have spent many years with wheat-maize rotation, so I will keep most of the land in that system because it is steady and fits my well irrigation. I will put 4.8 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 2.0 mu for cotton because I still want some cash income but I do not want too much labor pressure at my age.

For wheat, I will use improved seed rather than old saved seed because I want a more even stand and more stable yield. I will fertilize, but not push it too hard. I will give enough nitrogen for tillering and grain filling, add phosphorus for root growth, and some potassium to hold the crop steady. Since I have well irrigation, I will irrigate a few key times instead of watering too often. I will do rotary tillage because it is easier for me than deep ploughing and still prepares the seedbed well enough on my scale. I will spray only as needed, mainly to control weeds and common diseases.

For maize after wheat, I will continue on the same 4.8 mu. I will use hybrid seed because maize responds well and gives me stronger yield. I will feed it more nitrogen than wheat because maize needs it, with moderate phosphorus and potassium. I will irrigate at the important stages if rainfall is not enough. I will also keep rotary tillage because it is practical for me and saves effort. I will not chase maximum input; I will aim for a dependable harvest.

For cotton, I will keep it on 2.0 mu only. Cotton takes more attention, so I will not expand it. I will use improved seed, keep fertilizer moderate, irrigate several times because I have access to well water, and spray more times than wheat or maize because insects are usually more troublesome in cotton. I will still use rotary tillage because it reduces labor. My goal is not to take risks. I will manage for steady output that matches my age, my experience, my water access, and the size of my farm.
